title: spec_expose plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `spec_expose` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component SpecExposeConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

SpecExposeConfig.description: Plugin: spec_expose — Exposes API specification documents (OpenAPI, WSDL, WADL) for GET and HEAD on the canonical /specz sub-path. HEAD retains the GET representation through response-body policy, then returns the final status and representation headers without a wire body. Unauthenticated. Only works with prefix-based listen_path proxies (HTTP only). Successful upstream fetches are capped by max_response_body_bytes, decoded from origin Content-Encoding (gzip, x-gzip, br, identity) to identity bytes before cache and /specz, and cached in-process for cache_ttl_seconds (default 300s). Unsupported or malformed origin coding is HTTP 502. Failed fetches are coalesced and negatively cached with bounded exponential backoff; excess cache-miss waiters receive HTTP 503 with Retry-After.

spec_url.description: Full URL (http or https only) to fetch the API specification document (e.g., https://internal-service/docs/openapi.yaml). Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. The authority must be nonempty and must not contain userinfo ('@'). Paths and queries may be used for origin routing or signed access, but are omitted from gateway diagnostics. Remaining URL parse details (IPv6 literals, IDNA, percent-encoding) are runtime-only.

content_type.description: Trusted response Content-Type override; it is not restricted by the upstream allow-list. When set it must be nonempty after trim and a valid HTTP header value (HTAB and printable ASCII). When omitted or null, only supported spec media types are preserved from upstream (case-insensitive media-type comparison, with original parameters retained); every other or missing value falls back to application/octet-stream.

tls_no_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification when fetching the spec. Omitted or null defaults to the gateway's FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY setting. When verification is enabled and a gateway CA bundle is configured, load or parse failure rejects plugin construction instead of widening trust.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: Time-to-live for the in-process spec body cache (seconds). Omitted or null defaults to 300. The first /specz request fetches the spec from spec_url and stores the identity document; subsequent requests within the TTL window return the cached copy without re-fetching. Set to 0 to disable durable positive caching; callers admitted before an in-flight fetch completes still share that fetch regardless of scheduling delay, while later requests immediately re-fetch. Failed fetches use bounded negative-cache backoff regardless of this value.

max_response_body_bytes.description: Maximum upstream spec response body size to buffer, decode, and cache. Omitted or null defaults to 26214400. Must be greater than zero. The coded origin body is streamed with this cap, then decoded to identity under the same bound, so oversized or explosively compressed responses are rejected with HTTP 502 before unbounded memory growth.
